name: PixiTween Director S12e: crew replay, crew report and the demo film
description: Turn any finished crew film into a show: a replay of its event log in the studio view with the player following the versions, a 'Watch it being made' button in the gallery, a crew report that prints the measured numbers, the committed demo film fixture and docs/crew.md for the README.

userStories.title: Fetch a film's event log
userStories.description: As a replay, I want the whole event log of a film in one request so that it can be played back in order.
steps: Read server/http/handlers/crew.ts (GET /api/films/:id/log) and web/src/api/client.ts.
Create web/src/crew/replay/useEventLog.ts: useEventLog(filmId) fetches /api/films/:id/log once and returns { events, loading, error }, with no passcode header.
Add web/src/crew/replay/useEventLog.test.tsx with a mocked fetch.
acceptanceCriteria: useEventLog('f1') requests /api/films/f1/log exactly once and returns the events in the order received
A 404 response sets error 'not_found' and events []

userStories.title: Replay clock with speeds and gap compression
userStories.description: As a judge, I want the replay to keep the real rhythm but skip dead time so that a 2-minute build is watchable in under a minute.
steps: Read design.md section 8 and the event `at` timestamps in fixtures/s12d/crew-midbuild.json.

Create web/src/crew/replay/replayClock.ts exporting schedule(events, { speed: 1 | 2 | 4, maxGapMs = 1000 }) returning [{ event, atMs }] where each gap between events is divided by speed and then capped at maxGapMs.
Add web/src/crew/replay/replayClock.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Events at 0 s, 1 s and 21 s with speed 2 give atMs 0, 500 and 1500
The schedule keeps event order even when two events share a timestamp

userStories.title: useReplay drives crew state and the player by version
userStories.description: As a judge, I want the studio to look exactly as it did during the run so that the replay shows the real crew at work.
steps: Read web/src/crew/crewReducer.ts, web/src/crew/CrewStudio.tsx and GET /api/films/:id/versions.

Create web/src/crew/replay/useReplay.ts: given the events and the versions list, play the schedule with timers, folding events into crewReducer, and whenever a tool.call event carries a version, set the player composition to that version's composition. Expose play, pause, speed, progress and seek(fraction) (seek folds events up to that point).
Add web/src/crew/replay/useReplay.test.tsx with fake timers.
acceptanceCriteria: After playing the whole fixture, the crew state equals folding all events at once (deep equal) and the composition is the last version's
seek(0.5) yields the state of folding the first half of the scheduled events

userStories.title: ReplayBar in the studio and 'Watch it being made' in the gallery
userStories.description: As a judge, I want a button on each crew film in the gallery that replays how it was made so that I see the crew with no passcode and no cost.
steps: Read web/src/panels/Gallery.tsx and web/src/crew/CrewStudio.tsx.

Create web/src/crew/replay/ReplayBar.tsx (play/pause, 1x/2x/4x, progress scrubber, a 'Replay' badge) and edit web/src/crew/CrewStudio.tsx to accept a replay prop that feeds it from useReplay and hides every control that would post (chat, push-to-talk, card edits, cancel, pick).
Edit web/src/panels/Gallery.tsx: crew films get a 'Watch it being made' button that opens ?film=<id>&replay=1.
Add web/src/crew/replay/ReplayBar.test.tsx and extend the Gallery test.
acceptanceCriteria: With ?replay=1, CrewStudio renders no chat input, no push-to-talk and no Cancel or Pick buttons
A crew film in the gallery shows the 'Watch it being made' button; a non-crew film does not
Browser check: the replay of the fixture film plays to the end at 4x with the crew board lanes changing
Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

userStories.title: Crew report from an event log
userStories.description: As a owner, I want the crew's numbers printed from a real run so that the README and the video quote facts.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/08-agent-orchestration-review.md section 7 and scripts/cost-per-film.ts if it exists.

Create scripts/crew-report.ts: npx tsx scripts/crew-report.ts <data/films/<id>/events.jsonl> [--json] prints wall time to first playable scene, wall time to ready, showrunner turns and model, jobs by kind and status, peak parallel workers, superseded jobs, first-try tool-call validity, critic findings and fixes, cost by model and total, Clippy credits.
Add scripts/crew-report.test.ts over fixtures/s12e/crew-run.events.jsonl (a fake-mode run recorded by the test itself with the S12b fake showrunner).
acceptanceCriteria: The report over the fixture prints 'Peak parallel workers: 4' for the fake run with 4 overlapping builds
--json output parses and has numeric fields wallToReadySec and costUsd

userStories.title: Demo film fixture for offline replay
userStories.description: As a owner, I want a committed fake-mode crew film so that the replay and the gallery can be checked without any spend.
steps: Read server/crew/fake-showrunner.ts and server/store/film-store.ts (the data layout).

Create fixtures/s12e/demo-film/ holding a fake-mode crew film's film.json, versions/*.json, events.jsonl and its small fake assets, produced by a script step in scripts/crew-report.test.ts setup or a dedicated test helper, with no data: URLs over 200 characters.
Document in fixtures/s12e/README.md how to load it into DATA_DIR for a local replay.
acceptanceCriteria: fixtures/s12e/demo-film/events.jsonl contains at least one storyboard.revised event with source 'user' and one take.ready event
Loading the fixture into a temp DATA_DIR makes GET /api/films list it with crew true

userStories.title: docs/crew.md: how the crew works, for the README
userStories.description: As a judge, I want a short public explanation of the crew so that the technical depth is easy to verify.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/09-crew-swarm.md, design.md sections 3 and 5, and docs/architecture/README.md.

Write docs/crew.md: the crew table (lane, model, job), a mermaid diagram of inbox, showrunner, board and workers, the scheduling rules (4 workers, one writer per scene, user first, supersede with rollback), the blind critic, takes, the budget, how to replay a film, and a 'Measured' section with the crew-report numbers or 'to be measured'. Link call sites in server/crew/.
Add a docs check to scripts/crew-report.test.ts that docs/crew.md contains no 'docs/hackathon' or 'learn-improve' link.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/crew.md contains the headings 'The crew', 'How jobs run', 'Blind critic', 'Takes', 'Replay' and 'Measured'
docs/crew.md contains no link to docs/hackathon/ or docs/learn-improve/

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
Replay never calls a mutating route and never starts a model call: it reads /log, /versions and /assets only.
docs/crew.md must not link to gitignored paths (docs/hackathon/, docs/learn-improve/) and must quote only numbers that come from a recorded run, marking any missing number as 'to be measured'.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-5: owner picks the best MG-4 run, sets it as the gallery's featured film, and checks that its replay plays logged out on the deployed URL.
